summary: SSHConnection is the leaf connection wrapping paramiko.SSHClient. connect() lazily imports paramiko, loads system known hosts plus an optional KNOWN_HOSTS_FILE, applies a strict host-key policy (reject by default, warn, or auto_add) taken from the _post_connect envelope, and calls client.connect(**kwargs), mapping socket and paramiko failures to TransportConnectionError or ConnectionTimeoutError. It serves both SFTP storage and the tunnel bastion.
key_classes: SSHConnection — ConnectionProtocol leaf owning one paramiko.SSHClient
key_functions: SSHConnection(connect_kwargs: dict) — kwargs for paramiko connect plus a '_post_connect' dict (host_key_policy, known_hosts_file)
SSHConnection.connect() -> Self — host-key policy setup and authenticated connect; releases the client on any failure
extension_points: _HOST_KEY_POLICIES maps policy names to paramiko policy classes; must stay in sync with SFTPStorageProfile validation (sftp_storage_profile.py comment)
lifecycle_notes: paramiko is imported in connect(); missing paramiko raises TransportConnectionError naming [sftp].
Invalid host_key_policy raises ValueError before any socket is opened.
Partial acquisition is released on failure, with cleanup errors attached as notes.
__enter__ returns self without connecting; __exit__ disconnects and attaches cleanup failures as notes when the body raised.
documentation_hooks: SFTP/SSH host-key verification table (reject/warn/auto_add) and migration from 'ignore'
risks: 'warn' and 'auto_add' policies permit man-in-the-middle attacks (README host-key table); auto_add only remembers keys for the client lifetime.
Missing paramiko raises TransportConnectionError instead of MissingExtraError.
Host-key policy names are duplicated between ssh.py and SFTPStorageProfile; drift would cause late ValueErrors.
